Apple has once again stepped up to donate money in support of relief efforts following a deadly natural disaster. Here are the details.

Apple pledges support after deadly floods

Apple CEO Tim Cook announced tonight that the company will donate to support relief and reconstruction efforts in Nepal and Tibet, where a glacial lake outburst flood and landslides have killed hundreds of people.

The disaster began on Wednesday, when the lower section of a Himalayan glacier collapsed. Debris temporarily blocked a river before bursting, sending floodwaters and mud cascading downstream, killing hundreds of people, displacing large numbers of residents, and destroying villages, roads, bridges and other infrastructure.

Cook's pledge comes just days after Apple announced it would donate to support earthquake relief efforts in Indonesia, and in recent months the company has made similar donations in response to emergencies in Venezuela, Southern Europe and Japan.

Beyond responding to natural disasters and other emergencies, Apple also runs an internal donation programme called "Employee Giving," which has raised over US$880 million to date through a donation matching policy.
